rationale: H8 (reviews/hcl/master-review.md) — a latent defect, recorded as a robustness fix. The pre-filter paired a NAMED-child index with `fieldNameForChild`, which indexes over ALL children including anonymous tokens: for an `object_elem` shaped `[key, "=", val]` it returns "key", null, "val" at indices 0/1/2, so the loop (which probes 0 and 1) asked about the `=` token and applied the answer to `val`. Both outcomes were RIGHT, purely because every `object_elem` happens to have that shape — index 0 is always the key, and index 1 is never a second key. One token before the key and the key would be walked as a reference while the value was dropped. The fix reads the grammar's own `childForFieldName("val")`. This fixture pins all six key spellings the grammar admits (bare, quoted, parenthesised, nested, computed, and inside a tuple) so a change of shape cannot pass unnoticed.

forbidRelationships.note: `(var.d)` is the KEY of `paren` — a data key, not a reference. Emitting it is the pre-fix shape the false index pairing would produce.
`(format("%s", var.g))` is the KEY of `computed` — the value `var.h` is the reference, and it IS emitted (see expectRelationships)
